A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIPPER and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched across the substantial reorganization, including the previously unlabeled pick-and-place subgoal-distance panel.

before.justification: v2 reports original robotic simulation results, baseline comparisons, feasibility diagnostics, and hyperparameter ablations across four tasks.

after.justification: v4 reports original robotic simulation comparisons and ablations, including retained results, and adds preference-usage statistics.

M1.justification: v2 Equation 15 explicitly drops the current lower-level value V^L from the practical loss; v4 Equation 9 restores it, using the V^L−V_m^L gap. This changes practical regularization within the retained bilevel framework, higher-level DPO, lower-level SAC, and algorithm stages.

E1.justification: Both evaluate maze navigation, pick-and-place, push, and Franka kitchen under sparse rewards. Randomly generated four-room mazes remain documented in v4 Appendix A.7 despite removal of their explanation from the main experimental introduction.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain DIPPER-No-V, DPO-FLAT, SAGA, PIPER without HER, RAPS, HAC, HIER, DAC, and FLAT. The diagnostic comparisons also retain their comparator set. HIRO is newly discussed as an excluded alternative, not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: v4 Appendix A.6 retains v2's Push/Kitchen training totals of 1.3M/0.63M steps, while new Table 1 uses 0.775M/0.45M. It is unclear whether these represent revised budgets or different accounting scopes. Reported horizons, network sizes, metrics, and demonstration controls otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The regularization-weight and entropy-parameter sensitivity studies retain their tested values but contain revised curves: v2 Figures 5–6 become v4 Figures 4–5. v4 Appendix A.4 adds descriptive preference-usage accounting per million environment steps. The feasibility/Q diagnostics and successful-task visualization frames are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe Figure 2 as means with standard-deviation shading across five seeds. No additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Several learning curves change numerically. For example, Figure 2's DIPPER endpoints for pick-and-place and push are approximately 0.27 in v2 versus 0.32 in v4. Ablation curves also change, and Table 1 adds preference-usage entries. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains; the principal comparative conclusions remain similar.

T1.justification: v4 writes the general higher-level objective using the current lower-level policy before imposing optimality in the bilevel formulation. It also removes v2's nonnegative-reward/lower-bound argument for dropping V^L. The Bellman-to-DPO derivation is otherwise largely relocated and expanded into intermediate algebra in Appendix A.1, rather than replaced by a new proof.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces v2's claim of the first bilevel reformulation of HRL with a formulation tailored to goal-conditioned HRL. The central claims about preference optimization, feasible subgoals, non-stationarity mitigation, and up-to-40% improvement remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds an explanation of stationary preference labels based on fixed recorded states and discusses obsolete replay-buffer transitions. It explicitly identifies the preference data as automatically labeled rather than human annotated. The limitations concerning out-of-distribution generalization and high-dimensional subgoal spaces remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 leaves preference acquisition largely unspecified. v4 Section 4.3 documents reward-based primitive-in-the-loop labeling, and Appendix A.4 reports approximately 10,000 comparison pairs per environment. It also adds grid-search, value-update-frequency, supplementary-code, and future-release information. These substantially expand documentation of the central training signal, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds discussion and citations for HIDIO, HIPPO, and curriculum/teaching work by Narvekar and Stone and by Lewandowski and colleagues. These additions acknowledge related bilevel approaches and distinguish them from DIPPER, accompanying the narrower novelty claim. The broader related-work coverage remains intact.

P1.justification: Sections 3–5 undergo extensive editing and restructuring: the lower-level MDP now precedes the higher-level MDP, many numbered subsections become inline headings, and the derivation moves into an expanded appendix. Preference collection, ethics, and reproducibility sections are added. The title, author information, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The learning and ablation plots are redrawn with substantially larger axis labels and revised formatting. v2 Figures 3–4 become one eight-panel Figure 3, correcting the missing pick-and-place panel label. A preference-usage table is added, existing visualization frames are consolidated, and the document adopts a different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency by documenting preference construction and volume, narrows its novelty claim alongside relevant prior work, and improves figure legibility. These provide a limited net quality gain. Reproducibility remains incomplete: Table 1's step counts are not reconciled with Appendix A.6, and the new reproducibility statement incorrectly says Table 2 specifies λ and β.
